title: Occurrence and age‐specific dietary exposure assessment of chlorate, perchlorate, glyphosate, and glufosinate in infant, follow‐on, and young‐child formulas marketed in Türkiye
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

Formulas may be the main source of nutrition in early life, yet data on highly polar contaminants in formulas marketed in Türkiye are scarce. This study assessed the occurrence of, and dietary exposure to, chlorate, perchlorate, glyphosate, and glufosinate in 89 powdered formula samples covering three age-related stages (0–6, 7–12, and 13–36 months) using modified Quick Polar Pesticides Method extraction, EMR-Lipid clean-up, and liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry.

RESULTS

Chlorate was detected in all samples, with stage-specific mean concentrations of 91.23–126.25 μg kg−1 and a maximum of 414.23 μg kg−1. Perchlorate was quantified in 43.3–51.7% of samples, with mean concentrations of 9.58–24.95 μg kg−1 and a maximum of 97.03 μg kg−1. Deterministic exposure assessment under a conservative exclusive-formula-feeding scenario showed P95 chlorate estimated daily intakes (EDIs) of 4.68 and 4.77 μg kg−1 body weight (bw) day−1 in stages 1 and 2, corresponding to hazard quotients (HQs) of 1.56 and 1.59 against the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) tolerable daily intake (TDI) of 3 μg kg−1 bw day−1, whereas mean-based HQs remained below 1. The highest P95 perchlorate EDI was 0.97 μg kg−1 bw day−1 in Stage 1, yielding an HQ of 0.69 against the updated EFSA TDI of 1.4 μg kg−1 bw day−1. Glyphosate was rarely quantified, whereas glufosinate was not detected.

CONCLUSION

HQ values exceeding 1 indicate a potential toxicological concern rather than confirmed adverse health effects. Chlorate therefore represented the principal screening-level concern, particularly during the first year of life. The findings support continued monitoring and further investigation of process water, sanitation practices, and raw materials as potential sources. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
